By the numbers: Since February, Republican consumer sentiment has plunged 15.1 index points, from 97.1 to 82, according to the latest University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers data. Democratic sentiment has fallen just 1.6 index points, from 41.8 to 40.2.

Republican consumer sentiment fell 15.1 points from February to August 2026, while Democratic sentiment fell 1.6 points over the same period.
results.title: Republicans sour on the economy

results.content:
Just 8% of consumers in this month’s University of Michigan surveys expected their income growth to exceed inflation in the year ahead.

Decreases in sentiment were seen across the political spectrum in the most recent consumer index, but Republicans exhibited the strongest month-to-month decline.

Sentiment among Republicans is now 19% below readings just prior to the Iran conflict and the lowest since the 2024 election, according to Hsu. ## July 2026 LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index

Washington DC, July 10, 2026--The LSEG/Ipsos Primary Consumer Sentiment Index for July 2026 is at 51.0. Fielded from June 19 – 30, 2026, the Index is up 1.9 points from last month.

The index shows its first increase since January, ending a stretch that saw the index fall more than four points. However, it sits nearly three points below its reading from this time last year. Fielded from November 21 – 26, 2025, the Index is up 0.5 point from last month.

The index has increased slightly following last month’s decline.
